chapter: Thomas, own bands and neighborhood clubs
title: Dick Allen's first visit to New Orleans and hearing Barnes
summary: Allen tells of a weekend when he caught three bands, including Barnes's, and Friedwald recalls seeing Paul Barnes.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I think when I first came there, I came down here for the Sugar Bowl game the University of Georgia was playing here. What year? Well, I can look that up, but I don't know, 47 I think. Anyway, I can date it by that. I remember the game. And Amelia was there with Telfer then. You saw him the first night you were in town? No, no, no, no, first- Second- and dated by that, I remember the game. And Mealy was there with Telfer then.
You saw him the first night you were in town?
No, no, but the second one. See, first I called Rene, and then Rene told me about Big Eye Lewis, then I met this guy Art Schreiber there, and he told me about the hominé, and we went down there.
All in one night, all in that one weekend?

All in one, yeah. But I caught those three bands in one night. So they had some people here then, well, the Brian Derby on Canal Street was a dump where Rene was playing shows and stuff, and now Hutchins was where Big Eye was. Well, the Hall of Fame was kind of a nice place. Yeah.
It's fun. I don't believe they had a crowd, though.

I don't know. I don't know, I saw Cag and Paul Barnes there, he wasn't doing badly. No. Well, that was the job that you fixed up for Paul, I guess. You must have called you when you sent Paul, huh? Yeah. Well, you worked at any of these other little clubs, did you, really?
